speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; could you please detail your past medical conditions and when these balance issues first started?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; the "drunk" appearance suggests a significant issue with your cerebellum or the pathways connecting to it. You mentioned a significant medical history—could you please specify what past conditions you have, and has there been any history of trauma to your head or neck?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis presenting with cerebellar ataxia.

The patient's history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is a major risk factor for developing Multiple Sclerosis, and their symptoms are consistent with a relapse in the cerebellum. I will proceed to request MRI images of the brain and spine to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain, MRI Spine.
